**Why it is open**

**The engineering half is already ruled and needs no further work.** An independent Fable review agreed the
exemption is correct as an engineering matter, having verified across **all branches** that no commit has
ever registered `WoltMenuSyncBackgroundService` in either fully-qualified or short form — the only similar
hits are an unrelated `AddScoped` sync service, comments, and the lane's own driver.
**What makes this yours is the consequence, not the code.** `Services/WoltMenuSyncBackgroundService.cs:21`
runs on `TimeSpan.FromMinutes(8)`, so registering it begins live third-party menu pushes. That is a
decision about a partner relationship.
**Nothing is exposed while this waits.** The service cannot run, because it is registered nowhere; wiring
it without a ruling reds the floor's exemption fact; and a new unlisted loop reds the completeness fact.
Both directions were proven by mutation, not asserted.
**Fable recommends `keep-exempt`, and in doing so corrects a claim this plan has been carrying.** The
containment floor was recorded here as counting **types rather than registrations**, so that it would stay
green with every registration line deleted. **At the tip it reads `graph.Registrations` filtered on
`AddHostedService`** — the clerk verified the source directly — and a companion assertion re-derives every
parked exemption and fails one that becomes reachable.
**So this service is dormant *and guarded*, not dormant and forgotten**, and the control names its invoker.
That makes it one of the estate's two exceptions to its own disease rather than another instance of it.
**Registering it instead would add a production lever whose only consumer is a test, and whose fail-open is a
live eight-minutely push to a partner.**

**The options**

- `keep-exempt`
  - leave WoltMenuSyncBackgroundService on the written exemption list — pro: registering it starts live 8-minutely menu pushes to a third party, which is a commercial act and not an engineering one; the floor already reds both if somebody wires it and if the exemption goes stale, so it is dormant and guarded rather than dormant and forgotten
  - **con:** the one background loop touching an external partner is the one loop with no positive floor, so nobody is told the day it should have been running
- `register-and-gate`
  - register it, with the outbound push held behind a lever the test host keeps down — pro: the exemption list empties and all ten loops carry the same floor
  - **con:** it adds a production gate whose only consumer is a test, which is the shape C3 warns against, and a gate that fails open sends live pushes to a partner
- `retire-it`
  - delete the service if the Wolt menu sync is not a capability this product still intends — pro: an unregistered service that has never run on any branch is dead weight, and deleting it removes both the exemption and the question
  - **con:** irreversible without the Wolt owner, and the dormancy may be deliberate rather than abandoned

Ruled: keep-exempt 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: the Wolt owner declares menu sync a wanted capability, at which point register-and-gate with a positive floor on the lever

document, and until that lane landed, both arrived under **the same filename**, which is how the second one

**The filename half is fixed and is not what this decision is about.** Two credit notes against invoice
990601 now serve as `KREDITNOTA-990602` and `KREDITNOTA-990603`, proven from the host's own log rather than
from a test assertion. What remains is the product question the lane deliberately did not answer: whether
the second document should exist at all.
**Why it is yours.** Refusing it is a change to what the product will let a bookkeeper do, and partial
credits are a real workflow — this is not a defect with an obviously correct fix.
**Fable recommends `refuse-second`, and the con shielding the other option describes a workflow this product
cannot perform.** The clerk verified it directly: the creation method takes **only an invoice id**, copies
**every line**, and `IsCreditNote = true` appears in **exactly one file, once**. **There is no partial-credit
capability**, so "crediting two lines separately is legitimate practice" is not a description of this system.
**Every second credit note is therefore a full double credit of the whole invoice**, minted by one
double-click on a live production endpoint — and under C1 it exists forever with nothing warning anyone. **A
one-per-invoice check breaks nothing that exists.**
**This is the only live production surface in its whole set.**

**The options**

- `allow-and-number`
  - keep issuing, each under its own number, which is what now ships — pro: already built and pinned at the wire tier, partial credits keep working, and the two documents are distinguishable to a reader and to a filesystem
  - **con:** a double click still issues a real second statutory document that somebody must then void, and nothing warns the operator it happened
- `refuse-second`
  - reject a credit note against an invoice that already has one — pro: one invoice, one credit note is what an accountant expects, and an accidental double click cannot silently produce a second bokføring document
  - **con:** crediting two lines of one invoice separately is legitimate practice, so a blanket refusal breaks a real workflow to prevent a mis-click
- `allow-with-confirmation`
  - issue, but require an explicit confirmation when the invoice already carries a credit note — pro: keeps partial credits legal while making the second one deliberate rather than accidental
  - **con:** it is a UI change on a path that has none today, and a confirmation on a routine action is the kind people learn to click through

Ruled: refuse-second 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: a real line-subset credit-note capability lands, at which point allow-with-confirmation is the right shape and never allow-and-number

### D-SPEC-L-PROBE-DROP-CONSUMERWEB — the plan contradicts what L-PROBE-DROP-CONSUMERWEB observed

plan.md:20079

**Why it is open**

Removing a probe line and its fact span is a hand-edit of plan.md structure that no `plan` verb performs and that law L7 forbids a lane from making, contradicted by the CLI carrying no probe-mutation verb and by SPEC 1.2 assigning plan.md structure to humans.
**The lane was right to refuse, and it did the work anyway.** It extracted the verb set from the binary
rather than trusting `--help` — `init sign-off check refresh tick render serve headline start built verify
unverify accept retract decide flag note return log compact` — and **nothing mutates the probes fence.**
Every probe string in the tool is parse or validation. SPEC §1.2 assigns `plan.md` structure to humans;
§8 names the probes table as a hand-edited surface by design; L7's only exception is **additive**.
**A scope correction that changes the answer: two probes read that root, not one.**
`meals.token.client` (wire) and `cw.world` (meta). The ruling named the first. **Dropping only it leaves the
exit's second half false**, because `doctor` derives roots by grepping the whole fence and reads
`WORLD.json` from disk regardless.
**The order matters and was read off the tool, not guessed.** Span out first, line second, authored
references in the same edit: line-first raises `E-FACT-NO-PROBE`, a hard **error**; span-first degrades to
`W-PROBE-UNUSED`, a warning this plan already carries elsewhere.
**The item that makes this genuinely yours rather than clerical.** Dropping `meals.token.client` touches
five places — the probe line, the span, a `clears_when:`, a prose reference, and **the `exit:` of
`L-MEALS-FUNDED`, whose state is `verified`.** Rewriting a verified lane's exit changes what "verified"
meant for it. That is a judgement about evidence, not a deletion. Its other evidence half is a journey
artifact, so the real question is **whether that journey alone still carries the exit.**
**Census delivered regardless of the ruling — 33 probes over 3 roots**, and it separates checked-and-safe
from never-checked rather than reporting a single number: `.` — 8 probes, declared and conforming;
`../OkamAPI-modules` — 23 probes, declared but **MISMATCH**, which is the guard working and is already
ruled `already-guarded`; `../ConsumerWeb` — 2 probes, **UNDECLARED**, the only root that has never been
checked at all. **31 of 33 probes read a checked root**, and `MISMATCH` is not `UNDECLARED`.
**Fable recommends `clerk-does-it-both-probes`, and found the defect live on the board today.**
`fact:meals.token.client` is stamped **green as of 2026-08-04** on a root whose world **nobody declared** —
the clerk confirmed `on_expected` reads `unknown` on disk, and the doctor tags exactly that as undeclared. **A
green fact standing on unverified ground is this set's disease in its most direct form**, and
leave-both-and-restate would convert it into documentation.
**The cart-probe-only option measurably cannot meet the exit.** The genuinely owner-level part is that the
edit rewrites the exit of a lane already `verified` — that should be ruled explicitly as an evidence re-word,
in the measured order.
**Executed 2026-08-05 by the clerk, in the order the ruling specified.** Both fact spans removed first, both
probe lines second, and the two references rewritten in the same edit — the exit of the `verified` lane that
named the dropped fact, and a flag's clearing condition that read the same fact.
**The exit is met and was checked rather than assumed:** the doctor now lists two worlds and **no undeclared
root**. Before the edit, a fact was stamped green on a root whose world read `unknown`.
**The lane is retracted rather than dispatched**, because the ruling gave the work to the clerk and a session
spent re-deriving it would have produced the same three edits.
**One thing the same run surfaced and nothing had recorded:** the doctor reports the backend world as a
**MISMATCH** — the checkout sits on a lane branch, **missing four landed commits and carrying one unlanded**.
Every lane in this program has been told to read that repository with `git show <ref>:<path>` for exactly this
reason; **the mismatch is now visible in the instrument rather than only in the briefs.**

**What it is blocking**

- L-PROBE-DROP-CONSUMERWEB — ~~the plan stops claiming a fact it cannot ground~~ (retracted)
- F-PROBE-ROOT-WRONG-WORLD — the checkouts the facts are read from are not the world the plan declares · stays open while that lane waits

**The options**

- `clerk-does-it-both-probes`
  - retract the lane and have the clerk make the edit, dropping BOTH ConsumerWeb probes in the order the lane established: span out first, line second, authored references in the same edit — pro: it is the only route the tool's own ownership model allows, the order is measured rather than guessed, and it actually satisfies the exit's second half, which dropping one probe does not
  - **con:** it needs the clerk to hand-edit inside the probes fence, which L7 forbids without an explicit exception, so it is your permission to give and not the clerk's to assume; and it drags in the L-MEALS-FUNDED question below
- `clerk-does-it-cart-probe-only`
  - drop only `meals.token.client`, the probe the ruling actually named — pro: it stays inside the letter of `D-CONSUMERWEB-WORLD`, whose `reopen_when` speaks of restoring "the cart probe"
  - **con:** **measured, it does not work** — `plan-guards doctor` reads `WORLD.json` from disk rather than through the probe, so the root stays listed and still prints `UNDECLARED`, and the lane closes having changed nothing the exit asked for
- `leave-both-and-restate`
  - keep the probes and rewrite the exit to say the root is undeclared and known-unchecked — pro: nothing is edited inside the fence, and an honestly labelled gap is better than a silently missing check
  - **con:** the plan keeps a probe reading a world nobody declared, which is the condition the original ruling called out; it converts a defect into documentation

`artifacts/` was ignored as a **directory**, so git never descends and **no negation pattern could ever re-include it**; **nothing in either repository emits a trx or junit** (every `--logger trx` in the estate is prose *inside* a receipt, not a command anyone runs); and `jest-junit` is not installed. Nineteen uncommitted `.trx` files sit under `lanes/`, which is **not** gitignored. **The barrier was never technical — there was no rule saying which file, at which commit, is the record.**

**Fable recommends an option this block does not carry, and it should be written in before any ruling:
`forward-only-plus-C8`.** Neither existing option is what it would choose. **Retrofit is refuted by the lane's

recovery. And forward-only *without* the constraint is **literally the experiment that already failed on
2026-07-31.**
**What makes the third option different is that it names an invoker.** The brief generator copies intent
constraints verbatim into every brief, so a constraint reaches every future lane author by mechanism rather
than by their reading a README. **The roughly 361-branch backlog belongs as a dated note, not as fresh
receipts.**

- `forward-only-plus-C8`

  - **con:** it needs an intent amendment, which is yours alone, and it leaves ~361 existing branches with claims nobody can check
- `forward-only-no-C8`

  - **con:** **measured, the rule already existed and was already unfollowable** — a well-written convention sat unread at `artifacts/tests/README.md` since 2026-07-31 while seven incompatible variants were in use, so filing it again is the option that has already been tried
- `retrofit-anyway`
  - attach a receipt to each existing branch now — pro: the count of unbacked claims goes to zero
  - **con:** **it is the fabrication this lane exists to prevent** — a run executed today attached to an hours-old commit, and this lane's own two receipts differ by **36 tests at identical source** purely from harness state, so a fresh run demonstrably cannot stand in for the original
- `declare-the-backlog`
  - keep the forward rule and write the ~361 unbacked claims down as a known, dated gap — pro: honest and cheap, and it lets a reader tell which claims are checkable from which are not
  - **con:** a number that large in a document tends to be read once and never acted on

Ruled: forward-only-plus-C8 2026-08-06 by @sven

### D-EV-INQUIRY-UNGATED — whether a guest may raise an enquiry for a store that has not opened Events

plan.md:20215

**Why it is open**

**Raised because the flag it answers says outright that this is a product call, not a defect.** The lane
that gated accept and decline **deliberately left the public enquiry write alone** and said why — which was
the right call and is why there is a decision here rather than a fix.
**The harm as it stands:** a guest can create an event row for a store whose admin surface answers **404** —
**a confirmation for a booking the venue can never see.**
**The reason it is not simply a bug:** the enquiry form is plausibly how a venue discovers the module at
all, so refusing the write may close the front door on the thing that sells it.
**One thing already settled and not in question**, recorded so no option quietly reopens it: the same lane
**left the payment callback ungated on purpose**, because gating it would strand in-flight money, and that
posture is already documented against the deposits surface. Whichever option is ruled here, it does not
extend to the callback.
**Fable recommends `refuse-the-write` — and both halves are already built and idle.** A backend lane
implements exactly this option with a deliberately **uniform** refusal, so that one anonymous
sequential-id endpoint cannot be walked to enumerate which venues run Events, with 193 lines of gate tests; a
frontend lane withdraws the form on a standing refusal while surviving per-attempt ones.
**The lead-capture argument fails on the measured state.** Today's rows are a confirmation shown to the guest
and **silence at the venue** — nobody reads them, **so nothing is being captured.** Ruling this option means
adopting the built pair through the review protocol, not commissioning work.

**The options**

- `refuse-the-write`
  - gate the public enquiry write on the store's Events core flag — pro: no guest ever receives a confirmation for a booking the venue cannot see, which is the concrete harm today
  - **con:** it may close the front door on the thing that sells the module, since the enquiry form is plausibly how a venue discovers Events at all
- `unreachable-not-refused`
  - leave the write ungated but stop the form being reachable for an un-opted store — pro: the same harm is prevented without a refusal a guest experiences as a fault, and an un-opted venue simply has no public surface
  - **con:** reachability is a weaker guarantee than a gate — a stale link, a cached page or a direct POST still writes, so the harm returns by a quieter route
- `deliberate-and-recorded`
  - keep it open, and record in the plan that an enquiry for an un-opted store is intentional lead capture — pro: it is honest about what the form is for, and costs nothing to implement
  - **con:** somebody must then own what happens to those rows, because today they are a confirmation to a guest and silence at the venue

Ruled: refuse-the-write 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: a product decision gives enquiries from un-opted stores a real owner, such as routing them to sales

links hold, each of the six commits has exactly one parent, and `rev-list` counts exactly six over the modules
tip. **"Merging the head lands all six" is true for any completed merge, not only a fast-forward** — with
author resolution confined to the two money-path files the manifest names, re-measured exact. **And the reason
a peer list would triple-merge is now precise: the three deepest commits each exist under two ref names,

page declares no local `priceLabel` on either side. **Measured, not narrated.**
**The patch-id caveat is asymmetric, which rescues eight claims.** Rebase-blindness breaks only the *negative*
direction — a `+` does not prove absence — while a `-` is **positive evidence** an equivalent diff is already in
the target. All eight content-equivalence claims stand on that, and five of them rest on object ancestry where
patch-id plays no part at all.
**"Forty-five carry a real unlanded fix" is 43, or 44 if a comment correction counts.** One branch's entire

**Seven frontend heads created since the census cut are unclassified**, all of them lanes dispatched tonight.

drift**.
**All seven conditions applied, none refused, each re-measured by object before being written in — and the
re-measurement added three things the review had not found.**
**The old figure failed on its own arithmetic.** "19 of 25 conflict, 4 clean" does not add up, and nobody

recorded verdicts are 20 conflicts not 19, one head sat in the denominator while listed *not run* and conflicts

files.** **A landing plan sized on 19 is short by seven authored merges.** One of the four clean heads turns out

At its own base, `Program.cs` exposed exactly `"ETag"` and the constant that replaced it **did not yet exist**.
So the older commit **was correct where it was written** and is wrong only as a resolution against today's tip.
The rule now written in: **merge both, resolve to the newer side, and check it with a download arriving under a
readable filename.**
**The false edge is confirmed and it hid two family members**, not just one relationship — the commit joins two
steps later than drawn, at a merge the diagram omits entirely, and the conclusion it supports survives
re-verification.
**And the sentence about test evidence was a half-quote.** It cited a lane's message while **that same message

- `con: those authors' sessions have ended, so "the author" is a new agent reading someone else's diff. It is sixteen lanes, and this program has sixteen lanes of higher-value work queued behind them.`
- `one-rebase-lane`

- `con: one agent resolving sixteen unfamiliar conflicts is precisely what the composition brief forbids`

- `land-the-clean-thirty-five-first`

- `con: it moves our branch before the journey tier is green, and the standing instruction was to prove everything on the candidate before merging into anything else.`
- `drop-and-reauthor`
  - abandon the sixteen branches and rebuild their work against the current tip
- `pro: no conflict resolution at all. Each lane re-proves its own exit against a tip that exists, which is the only thing that has reliably worked here.`
- `con: it discards work that was built and in some cases reviewed, and it repeats effort that a rebase would have preserved.`

### D-WF-INVITE-LANDING-PAIR — a capability built on two branches, neither landed, both clean fast-forwards

**Why it is open**

enumerated and their route attributes read at `8e2b57de` **by object**, not from the stale checkout. The manager
side has `POST staff/{id}/invitations` and nothing else; there is **no list route and no revoke verb anywhere.**
`IWorkforceInvitationService` declares exactly two methods, so this is a real absence and not an unwired
capability. `WorkforceInvitationState.Revoked = 3` exists in the enum and is written by no code path.

known issue route, and it surfaced `MealsMembershipController`'s list/create/revoke, the Company Meals trap that
does not answer a workforce question.
**It also verified the actionable half of the sentence**, which is what a manager acts on: reissue supersedes in
place at `WorkforceInvitationService.cs:117-125`, overwriting `TokenHash` on the single pending row, so the
previous token genuinely dies the instant a new one is minted. **The string steers toward the correct remedy.**
**Both pins were found, and the second only by searching the prose** — `test/workforce-roster-components.test.js:412`
is an assertion; `test/e2e/journeys/workforce-invitation-onboarding.spec.js:349` carries no key, is a finding note
rather than an assertion, and so **repeats the claim on every run without being able to red.**
**The moment either half lands, the sentence becomes false and must go with it.** That coupling is why this is one
decision rather than two. It is a separate question from `D-INTEGRATION-FASTFORWARD`, which is about the migration
stack rather than about a capability.

**The options**

- `land-both`
  - merge backend `lane/wf-invite-list-revoke` and frontend `lane/fe-wf-invite-list-revoke`, then retire the three locale strings and their two pins in the same act
- `pro: the capability becomes real for an operator, and the sentence that currently tells a manager it does not exist goes at the same moment, so the product never says one thing while doing another. Both are clean fast-forwards, independently verified with --is-ancestor in each repository.`
- `con: it is a simultaneous cross-repo landing on two shared branches, which is the act reserved to you. And the frontend branch has never been reviewed`
  - its return was refused on a format placeholder and its author was lost, so 23 files and +1684 lines have no reviewed record.
- `review-then-land`
  - a Fable review of both branches first, then land the pair
- `pro: it closes the gap above; the frontend half is the largest unreviewed diff in this program, and it inverts two existing pins rather than deleting them, which is exactly where a reviewer earns its keep.`
- `con: another cycle before an operator can revoke a code sent to the wrong person, and the branches drift further from their tips while it happens.`
- `land-backend-first`
  - merge the backend half now, hold the frontend
- `pro: it is the safe serialisation. The backend alone adds two routes nothing calls, which is inert; the frontend alone would bind buttons to routes that 404. If only one can move, this is the one.`
- `con: it leaves the three locale strings true-but-about-to-be-false, and a half-landed capability is the state this estate has been bitten by repeatedly`
  - proven work on a branch nobody merges.
- `leave-both`
  - keep the branches unmerged and the strings as they are
- `pro: the strings are accurate today; the lane verified that, and honest disclosure is better than a broken capability.`
- `con: the work exists and helps nobody, and every day it sits the two branches diverge from tips that are moving under them.`

Ruled: review-then-land 2026-08-05 by @sven

### D-MIG21-WHICH-TRIGGER-WINS — two migration files claim MIG-21 and the second one to run fails hard

plan.md:20547

**Why it is open**

**This is the only case in the estate where two real migration files claim one number**, found by a census of 28
numbers across 317 backend heads. `a6a1174b` / `20260731203011` against `23f6bbeb` / `20260801102621`, **neither
an ancestor of the other.**
**The two files differ by an eight-line comment.** Same `CREATE TRIGGER`, same `THROW 50060` and `50061`. It
would be tempting to call that harmless.
**It is not, because neither carries an `IF OBJECT_ID` guard.** Landing both does not apply the same DDL twice
to no effect — **the second `Up()` fails hard**, on whichever database replays the chain, which is a fresh
database and never the author's.
**Why it needs a person.** Every option deletes somebody's commit or changes a shape nobody agreed to. The
clerk may not drop a lane's work, and the third option trades a loud failure for a quiet one, which is a
judgement about what this estate wants to be told.
**Fable recommends `keep-23f6bbeb`, and the con protecting the other side is measured false.** The lane whose
id would be dropped is **exactly one commit ahead** of its merge-base, and that commit's entire payload — same
nine files, same tests, trigger body verbatim — **was already regenerated on the chain tip**, by a commit
whose own migration file documents the supersession: the lane's id would have forked the Designer parent and
broken fresh replays. **Nothing of the author's work dies except the stale id.**
**`guard-both` is the C1-hostile option**: it trades a loud failure for a silent one **on the fiscal-trigger
chain where this estate already shipped RF-1313.**
**One nit for the record:** this block's prose names a different migration file than the one that is actually
duplicated in that tree. **The ruling resolves the same way**, but the citation is wrong.

**The options**

- `keep-23f6bbeb`
  - land the later file and drop `a6a1174b`'s from the stack
- `pro: it is the one on the chain the other thirteen stacked branches descend from, so keeping it leaves the ten-link chain intact and touches nothing else.`
- `con: it drops a commit off `lane/margin-finalize-lag` that its author has not been asked about, and that branch may carry other work that assumes its own file is present.`
- `keep-a6a1174b`
  - land the earlier file and drop the other
- `pro: it is the original; the later one is the duplicate that appeared afterwards.`
- `con: it is off-chain, so keeping it means renumbering or re-parenting the chain that already descends from the other`
  - the expensive direction.
- `guard-both`
  - add `IF OBJECT_ID` guards so either order is survivable, and land both
- `pro: it removes the hard failure without anybody having to choose whose commit dies, and a guarded trigger creation is defensible on its own terms.`
- `con: it leaves two migrations claiming one number, which is the condition that produced this, and a guard that makes a collision survivable makes the next one silent.`

Ruled: keep-23f6bbeb 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: a commit appears on the losing lane beyond its current tip that depends on the dropped migration id — none exists today

### D-MEALS-MEMBERS-READ-LANDING — the dangerous half is already composed, and not deciding chooses it

plan.md:20594

**Why it is open**

**A real pair, unlike the two asserted earlier tonight, and measured rather than assumed.** Backend
`lane/meals-members-read` at `086ac34f` is 1 ahead and 0 behind — a clean fast-forward. The frontend half at
`9fbed80` is 4 ahead and 2 behind. `ListProgramMembersAsync` lives on exactly one api ref.
**The four combinations collapse to three, and on the opposite axis from the one the clerk guessed.** *Neither*
and *backend alone* are the same world, not *neither* and *frontend alone*: the enrolment control **arrives
entirely with the frontend half**, so the integration branch has **zero** enrolment hooks against eight on both
frontend refs. Backend alone is a dead route and an error code no web ref renders — invisible and harmless.
**Frontend alone is the dangerous world, and it does not look broken.** Twelve of thirteen routes exist, so the
programmes table fills with real data. Beneath it the manager reads *"Tick everybody who should be enrolled"* —
unconditional, no `v-if` — above boxes that are not there; *"Reload and try again"* for a route that will never
exist; and *"This server did not answer as Company Meals. We do not know whether the module is here."* **They
are told the module may not be installed while looking at its data, and they reload forever.** Not a data-loss
risk; the control is genuinely withheld.
**The note was replaced, not deleted, and that is worse.** `meals_enrol_no_read_note` became
`meals_enrol_unread_note` — **a permanent absence wearing a transient face, with a retry instruction attached.**
**Not deciding decides.** `2e3f39d` is already merged into `candidate/fe-compose-2026-08-05`; the api half is
merged nowhere. **The composed state is the dangerous one.**
**And no guard catches it.** The members read is deliberately unanchored in the divergence check, and the
journey's fixture defaults to answering a route the merge candidate lacks. **Green in CI, self-contradicting on
screen.**
**Symmetry with the workforce invite pair: inverted.** That pair's quiet half is *frontend* alone; this pair's
quiet half is *backend* alone. Each pair's dangerous direction is the other's safe one — **and this one's
dangerous direction is the one already composed.**
**One refinement from the branch manifest, which traced the failure rather than assuming it.** The panel maps
the missing GET to `DATA_UNKNOWN` and **withholds the enrol control** — so on the data side that direction is
**loud and safe**, not silent. That agrees with this decision's own measurement, which says the control is
genuinely withheld and no data is at risk.
**The two readings differ only in what "dangerous" names.** The manifest is describing the data path; this
decision is describing what a manager reads — *"Tick everybody who should be enrolled"* above absent boxes, and
a retry instruction for a route that will never exist. **Both are true: the control is safe and the copy is
misleading**, and it is the copy that costs an operator their morning.

**The options**

- `land-both`
  - merge backend `lane/meals-members-read` and keep the frontend half in the composition
- `pro: it is the only combination in which what the manager reads is true. The backend half is 1 ahead and 0 behind`
  - a clean fast-forward — and the frontend half is already merged into the candidate, so this is the smaller of the two remaining acts.
- `con: it is a cross-repo landing on a shared branch, which is yours; and the backend half has not been reviewed.`
- `unstage-the-frontend`
  - take `2e3f39d` back out of the composition candidate and land neither for now
- `pro: it restores the only other honest world. With neither half, there is no enrolment section at all, and nothing on screen claims one exists`
  - the manager is not told anything false.
- `con: it removes a built and mutation-proved capability from a candidate that took 35 merges to assemble, and it must be redone later anyway.`
- `land-frontend-only, deliberately`
  - accept the composed state and record why
- `pro: nothing else in the candidate has to move, and the panel's data half works: the programmes table fills with real Company Meals data.`
- `con: this is the state described below, in which the product tells a manager to reload forever for a route that will never exist. Choosing it deliberately at least puts the cost on the record instead of leaving it to a default.`

Ruled: land-both 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: the review of the single backend commit finds something, in which case unstage temporarily rather than let the composed state reach the shared branch

### D-GR-WITHDRAW-PAIR — a third pair, and the shipped half is the loud one

plan.md:20654

**Why it is open**

**Found by the branch manifest as the third must-land-together pair, and it is the worst-shaped of the three.**
`fe-gr-withdraw-origin` and `fe-growth-prefcentre` are **in the candidate**; the backend halves are **in neither
anchor**.
**The backend is the quiet half, which inverts the other two pairs.** Without it the failure is a
**credentialed-CORS preflight refusal** — no status code, no server log line, no rendered refusal, **on a
consent-withdrawal path**, and **no test reds either way**. A person clicks withdraw and nothing happens.
**Both authors independently reached the same conclusion**, in lanes that never communicated: shipping one half
alone leaves the page exactly as broken.
**And it carries a duplicate-fix hazard that a merge would not surface.** The CORS policy exists as **two
commits with an identical subject and distinct patch-ids** — `2a052800` (2026-08-03 11:22) and its rebase
`3c71b323` (2026-08-04 20:24). The clerk verified both. **Merging `lane/cors-followups` and
`lane/gr-withdraw-origin` lands the same change twice.** The manifest's recommendation is to take
`cors-followups` and drop the other four for that change — **a de-duplication by timestamp would not have found
it**, since the timestamps differ by a day while the subjects match exactly.
**The duplicate is not a duplicate, and that turns the dedup advice into a correctness requirement.** The
clerk verified both lines: `2a052800` writes `.WithExposedHeaders("ETag")`; `3c71b323` writes
`.WithExposedHeaders(BrowserReadableHeaders.All)`, **and its own doc-comment records that the hardcoded literal
silently dropped `Content-Disposition` and `X-Meals-Content-Hash`.**
**So the earlier commit is not merely redundant — it is wrong**, and the manifest's advice to *"take
`cors-followups` and drop the other four"* **cannot be followed as written**, because `lane/gr-withdraw-origin`
carries `2a052800` and **is this pair's backend half.** It cannot be dropped.
**The resolution rule, therefore:** when both land, `Helpers/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` must resolve to
`3c71b323`'s side — **never the hardcoded literal.** A merge that takes the older side restores a header
suppression nobody would see, on the paths that download documents.
**Fable's cross-cutting finding, 2026-08-05: the three landing pairs are one shape and must not get one
ruling, because their dangerous directions differ.** Two of the three frontend halves are **already composed
into the candidate**; the third is not.
**Meals and Growth therefore gate the candidate landing.** Their frontend halves are in the composition, so
their backend halves must be on the backend tip **before or with** the candidate, or landing ships a
self-contradicting Meals panel and a **silent consent-withdrawal refusal** — no status code, no log line, no
rendered refusal, no red test — onto the shared branch. **In both, not deciding chooses the harmful world.**
**The invite pair is the opposite case and the only one that genuinely needs a review first.** Its frontend
half is **not** composed, so nothing dangerous is live, and it is the largest unreviewed diff in the program —
23 files, roughly 1,700 lines — and it inverts two pins. There is no urgency to justify landing that unread.
**One resolution rule must be pinned wherever the Growth halves land:** the shared service-collection file
resolves to the newer commit's header allowlist, **never** the older literal — the older one silently drops
two headers, so it is wrong rather than merely duplicate.

**The options**

- `land-the-backend-halves`
  - merge the two backend halves so the frontend already in the candidate has something to talk to
- `pro: it is the only combination where consent withdrawal works. Both authors independently wrote that shipping one half alone leaves the page exactly as broken, which is unusual agreement between lanes that never spoke.`
- `con: it is a cross-repo landing on a shared branch, and it carries the duplicate-CORS hazard below, so it cannot be done by merging every branch that touches the policy.`
- `unstage-the-frontend`
  - take the two frontend halves back out of the candidate
- `pro: restores a coherent world where the withdrawal page is absent rather than silently refused.`
- `con: removes work already composed, and must be redone.`
- `land-nothing-yet`
  - accept the composed state and record it
- `pro: nothing has to move while the other five decisions are open.`
- `con: the composed state is a consent-withdrawal path that refuses **with no status code, no server log line and no rendered refusal**`
  - and no test reds either way.

Ruled: land-the-backend-halves 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: the withdrawal page turns out to be feature-hideable in the candidate more cheaply than the backend halves can land

### D-SPEC-L-ARM-RECEIPTS-RECAPTURE — the plan contradicts what L-ARM-RECEIPTS-RECAPTURE observed

plan.md:20721

**Why it is open**

**The lane ruled rather than improvised, and its reading is right.** `journey.js:657` resolves `servingFixture`
**only when `backend === "fixture"`**, with a documented rationale: a live API's working directory is not this
checkout by design, so identity for live worlds belongs to `backendBuild`. **All ten arm-N receipts are
`backend: "live"` by arm assertion**, and the stand-in API 404s the health endpoint on purpose — measured
`identitySource: "none"` on all ten.
**The clause is the clerk's error, and its origin is specific.** It was generalised from the artifacts census's
five re-runs, **which were all fixture-backed.** It does not survive contact with this receipt family.
**Three of the four exit clauses are met and the ten receipts exist**, taken from a clean worktree detached at
`7030c00` with `porcelain` empty before and after every run, both provers re-measured by the lane itself —
10 of 10 and 5 of 5, twice — each printing the ref's own `journey.js` sha and a build id with no `+dirty`.
**The first pass did print `+dirty`, and the instrument caught its own operator.** Two untracked run logs
written *inside* the worktree were enough. **That is a live hazard for any lane filing evidence into the
checkout it measures**, and it is the reason this one's output was moved out and the run repeated.
**What the re-capture found is the substance, and it is the first direct evidence of what the dead guard let
through.** Ten of ten differ, and two differences are real:
- **Both arm-3 originals name a build nobody can check out** — `Web-modules@…+dirty`, twice. The prefix is the
  port holder's directory basename, so **both were captured from the shared main checkout, dirty.**
- **Five receipts carry fields that exist in `journey.js` at none of the relevant refs.** Their sole producer is
  a commit on a lane branch that is **not an ancestor** of the ref they were committed to. **They were captured
  by a harness that is not on the branch they were filed into, by a tree that cannot emit their fields.**
**And the reassuring half, which matters as much:** the probe substance is **identical across all ten pairs** —
status, backend, surface, capabilities, findings, error and all three served-counters. **Only provenance moved.**
The captures were right and unwitnessed, exactly as the census framed it.
default_if_unruled: none
reopen_when: the ledger and per-backend run joins demonstrably cannot survive an exit re-word
journey.js:657 resolves servingFixture only when backend=="fixture"; all ten arm-N receipts are backend=="live" by arm assertion, so "each carrying servingFixture resolved to this run's own fixture" is unmeetable at 7030c00 without editing the journey.js sha both provers testify to.
**Fable recommends `respec-per-backend`.** At the receipts' own ref the harness resolves the serving fixture
**only when the backend is the fixture**, with the live-world rationale written in place — identity for a live
world belongs to the build stamp. **So the clause is unmeetable as written**, and accepting as built would
leave an exit in the plan that **no live-backed receipt can ever satisfy**: a written expectation that gates
nothing, this set's defect in prose form.
**Extending the harness instead would invalidate the ten recaptured receipts** and every green measured
against the sha both provers testify to. The work is done; only the wording is wrong.

**What it is blocking**

- L-ARM-RECEIPTS-RECAPTURE — ten receipts the repair just made re-capturable (built)

**The options**

- `accept-as-built`
  - treat the clause as satisfied by backendBuild for live-backed receipts and close the lane
- `pro: the design is deliberate and documented at journey.js:657`
  - a live API's working directory is not this checkout, so identity for live worlds is backendBuild's job, and backendBuild is exactly what caught the two arm-3 originals naming a build nobody can check out.
- `con: it leaves two different provenance contracts in the plan, and the next lane reading the exit will have to rediscover which family it is in.`
- `respec-per-backend`
  - rewrite the exit so a receipt names its fixture when fixture-backed and its backendBuild when live-backed
- `pro: it states the real contract instead of one family's version of it, and it is what the clerk should have written; the census's five re-runs were all fixture-backed and the clause was generalised from them.`
- `con: re-pointing an exit breaks the joins the ledger and the runs/ records use, and the lane has already done the work either way.`
- `extend-the-harness`
  - make servingFixture resolve for live backends too, then re-capture
- `pro: one provenance field for every receipt, and no reader has to know which family they are looking at.`
- `con: it means editing the journey.js whose sha both provers testify to, which invalidates the ten captures just taken and every green measured against that ref. The lane refused to do this unasked, correctly.`

Ruled: respec-per-backend 2026-08-05 by @sven

today across 172 of 607 files. Arming the gate turns every commit in every worktree red until those are fixed —
of which `curly`, `arrow-parens` and one Vue formatting rule are three quarters, and mostly auto-fixable.
**Fable recommends `remove`, having established the hooks are inert everywhere rather than merely unused
here.** 33 entries, husky v4 shims stamped from **a different repository's** node_modules — one lane's
accidental install — with **no `husky` key, no `.huskyrc`, and no branch in the estate's whole history that
ever configured hooks.** Removal therefore changes behaviour in no worktree, and the shims are two-line files
any reinstall recreates, so it is not irreversible either.
**Repair is the option that looks responsible and is not:** it would arm a gate nobody scheduled, on a tree
where three spot-checked files already carry 29 errors. **And leave-and-record keeps decoration that looks
like enforcement** — the precise defect this set indicts.

**The options**

- `remove`
  - delete the hooks from the shared common directory
- `pro: they do nothing today and they look like enforcement to anyone reading the tree, which is worse than no hooks. They were installed by one lane's `npm install` rather than by anybody's decision.`
- `con: deleting shared state that ninety worktrees see is irreversible from any single lane's position, and if anyone is relying on a hook that does work, it goes with them.`
- `repair`
  - make them fire, so the configured lint-staged runs
- `pro: it is what somebody once intended; `lint-staged` is configured and the rules are already at error.`
- `con: **it arms a lint gate across the entire estate on the strength of one lane's dependency install**`
  - and the repository currently reports 678 errors, so every commit anywhere would start failing at once.
- `leave-and-record`
  - keep them and write down that they are inert
- `pro: no shared state changes while eight other decisions are open, and the misleading appearance is at least documented.`
- `con: the next person to read `.git/hooks` still believes there is a gate, which is the condition that produced this.`

Ruled: remove 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: any branch is found whose package.json defines husky hooks — a search across all refs found only the initial commit

### D-RECEIPT-MODAL-UNTESTABLE — a component no test can mount, and a template rewritten to change that

plan.md:20828

**Why it is open**

**Raised by the lane itself rather than absorbed, which is why it is here.** `components/molecules/ReceiptModal.vue`
**could not be mounted in jest at all** — the transform cannot parse optional chaining — so the lane rewrote
**two template lines** to make its seven assertions possible. All seven red when the German dictionary is
reverted.
**The act is the question, not the lines.** A copy-correction lane changed production markup to enable a test.
**That is a different kind of change from the one it was dispatched for**, and it should be ruled rather than
noticed later in a diff.
**And the surface is the reason it matters both ways.** A receipt is a kassasystemforskrifta artifact. **It is
also, until now, a surface no test could mount** — which is how a German label naming the wrong issuing
authority survived on it, one line above a second string naming the wrong register.
**Fable recommends `accept-the-rewrite`, and names what the ruling should open beside it.** The template
transpiler genuinely cannot parse optional chaining, the two-line rewrite is behaviour-identical for every
value the field can hold, and seven mounted assertions all red on a dictionary revert. **The surface is a
kassasystemforskrifta artifact that no test could mount — which is how a German authority label survived on
it.**
**Fixing the toolchain instead is an unmeasured change under 878 files with no CI suite to catch what it
breaks.** But per-component rewrites do not scale, and **three further unmountable templates are already
named**, so the recommendation is to ratify these two lines and open a separate toolchain lane for the rest.

**The options**

- `accept-the-rewrite`
  - keep the two template lines the lane changed and treat optional chaining as unavailable in this component
- `pro: it is the smallest change that makes the surface testable at all, and the surface is a receipt`
  - the one artifact an inspector reads. Seven assertions now exist where none could.
- `con: a production template was changed to enable a test, which is an act this lane was not authorised for and which nobody reviewed as a product change.`
- `revert-and-lose-the-assertions`
  - restore the template and accept that the receipt cannot be mounted
- `pro: no production line moves for a test's convenience, and the copy fix stands on its own.`
- `con: the receipt modal then remains a surface **no test can mount at all**, which is how a mislabelled identifier survived on it in the first place.`
- `fix-the-toolchain`
  - make the transform accept optional chaining, then revert the template
- `pro: it removes the constraint rather than working around it, and any other component with the same syntax becomes testable too.`
- `con: it is a build-tooling change with an unmeasured blast radius across 878 files, and nothing in this repository currently runs a suite in CI to catch what it breaks.`

Ruled: accept-the-rewrite 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: a template-transpiler upgrade is measured green across the full suite, at which point revert the rewrite and take the toolchain

### D-OFFER-MONTHLY-ABSENCE — how an offer line says it has no monthly fee

plan.md:20929

**Why it is open**

**A consequence of a fix, reported rather than hidden.** With the offer document now refusing to total what
it cannot total, a **mixed** offer's monthly total reads `—`. The document **cannot tell "not applicable"
from "not stated"**: a one-time-only product's `enableMonthlyFee` lives on the catalogue item and never
reaches the document, so a line with no monthly fee by design is indistinguishable from a line whose
monthly fee somebody forgot to enter.
**Both readings are wrong in different directions, which is why this is a fork and not a lane.** Showing
`—` treats a deliberate absence as a gap. Showing a total resumes the behaviour just removed — presenting
a partial sum as a whole one. **There is no option here that is merely more work than the other; they
disagree about what the document is allowed to claim.**
**Whichever is chosen, the write-side rule holds:** the closing distinction is `=== null`, not falsiness,
because `!0` is `true` and a truthiness guard swallows the genuine zero — the case that must survive.
**Fable recommends `document-gets-the-flag`, and this page's own post-mortem is the argument.** The offers
page only offers a monthly-fee input when the catalogue item enables one, so **absence-by-design is
structural** — and the comment left on that very file records that the deleted helpers' defect was collapsing
**"stated, zero, absent — three worlds into one answer."**
**`line-writes-zero` re-creates that collapse at write time, permanently**, by manufacturing a value the
operator never entered. Carrying the flag lets the document say *not applicable* honestly **and** keep
refusing genuinely unstated fees — the two things the surface has to distinguish.

**The options**

- `line-writes-zero`
  - **pro:** the document needs no new input and the change is one write site
  - **con:** a real zero and a deliberate absence become the same value forever, so the distinction can never be recovered later
- `document-gets-the-flag`
  - **pro:** keeps not-applicable and not-stated genuinely distinct, which is what the surface has to say
  - **con:** the catalogue flag has to travel with every line, touching the contract between catalogue and document

Ruled: document-gets-the-flag 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: the offer-line contract turns out to be consumed by an external schema that cannot gain a field — and even then, version it before forging zeros

### D-SPEC-L-PAYMENTTYPE-FROM-CLIENT-UNGUARDED — the plan contradicts what L-PAYMENTTYPE-FROM-CLIENT-UNGUARDED observed

plan.md:20963

**Why it is open**

**The brief was wrong about reachability and the lane proved it rather than arguing.** It said
`FinalizeService.cs:501/:637` take `PaymentType` straight off a client DTO. **Those two request types are
never model-bound** — neither appears among the 250 `[FromBody]` types in the tree — and **all four
production callers pass server-derived values**: two hard-code `Cash` on DTOs that have no PaymentType
property at all, and two pass a transaction value set from a compile-time constant.
**The mechanism is real and was executed, not reasoned about.** With the enum and the six label and layout
functions copied verbatim from the tip and run twice byte-identically, an out-of-range value prints **the bare
decimal number**: `999` renders as the digits, twenty-three spaces, then the amount. No exception, no blank.
The app's own binder was proved to **accept** `999`, `7` and `"999"`, rejecting only unknown *names*.
**What is actually latent, and why it is worth a ruling rather than a shrug.** The card-sale finalize path
rejects only `NotSet`, so an out-of-range value would pass it — latent today because its sole caller passes a
constant. And the journal's payment type is persisted **as a string**, so such a value would sit as `"999"`
permanently on an **append-only** table. **C1 is what makes this a decision instead of a cleanup**: there is
no later repair for a row that should never have existed.
**Fable recommends `guard-where-the-value-enters`, placed as a service invariant rather than DTO attributes —
and it sharpens what the sibling landing does and does not close.** The shared label table now covers all 17
members with an `Ukjent` default, **which kills the "must be done twice" con of the builder option** — but it
**touches no finalize file at all**, so the C1 half is untouched: the journal still persists the type as a
string on an append-only table.
**The advertised-and-gates-nothing objection applies to attributes on never-model-bound DTOs, not to a service
invariant every present and future caller must pass.** And a payment type reaching paper as a C# identifier is
**this codebase's own proof that it adds enum members without revisiting consumers.**
**Its warning about closing this as unreachable is the sentence to keep:** with the label table merged, that
option **protects the paper and not the journal.**

**What it is blocking**

- L-PAYMENTTYPE-FROM-CLIENT-UNGUARDED — an undefined payment type cannot reach a printed fiscal line (built)

**The options**

- `close-as-unreachable`
  - **pro:** no code moves, and the guard that matters already exists — the settlement allocation whitelist throws "Unsupported payment type for a settlement allocation" before any row is written, and the one client-bound kassa DTO carrying a PaymentType dies there
  - **con:** it leaves two latent paths standing, and one of them writes to an append-only table, where a wrong value cannot be repaired afterwards
- `guard-where-the-value-enters`
  - **pro:** matches the IsDefined precedent already sitting on this same document's reason labels, and closes the latent card-sale path that today rejects only NotSet
  - **con:** the two Finalize DTOs are never model-bound, so a guard on them is a control on a surface no client posts to — the advertised-and-gates-nothing shape this plan has recorded three times in two days
- `guard-at-the-builder-default`
  - **pro:** closes every caller at once, including any future one, at the point where the wrong value becomes a printed byte
  - **con:** it must be done twice because the X/Z builder holds a byte-identical copy of the ladder, and it converts a data defect into a display fix — the journal would still carry "999" forever

Ruled: guard-where-the-value-enters 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: the latent class is judged not worth a guard — in which case closing it as unreachable must at least merge the landed label table

### D-TYPECHECK-IN-THE-BUILD — whether the shipping build type-checks

plan.md:21008

**Why it is open**

**`nuxt.config.js:37` sets `typeCheck: false`, so the shipping build is transpile-only** and cannot see a
semantic diagnostic. A duplicated translation key is therefore **completely silent in the build**, while the
test tier fails loudly on the same input. **The build actively preserves the duplicate**, rewriting the
literal so the later entry wins.
**The lane that measured this deliberately did not pull the lever, and was right not to.** Both directions
were measured, the cost is one line, and the blast radius is every worktree currently in flight — which makes
it a call about when, not about whether it works.

**The options**

- `turn-it-on`
  - **pro:** measured in both directions on this branch — the pristine tree stays exit 0 at effectively the same build time, and a planted duplicate exits 1 with exactly one diagnostic naming the file and line, so the class this plan has chased for two days becomes impossible to ship
  - **con:** it changes the integration branch's gate under roughly 130 in-flight worktrees at once, and any pre-existing type error anywhere in the tree becomes a build failure for every one of them on the same day
- `leave-it-off-and-guard-in-the-suite`
  - **pro:** the check already exists there, `npm test` is the only runner this repository actually executes, and nothing in flight changes
  - **con:** the guard then lives in a tier a release can skip, and the shipping build stays permanently blind to a semantic class it could catch in one line

Ruled: turn-it-on 2026-08-05 by @sven

Reopen when: a composed candidate carrying the outstanding merges shows pre-existing semantic diagnostics, or build time lands far beyond the measured half-again

### D-ACK-RECEIPT-IS-STATE-OR-EVIDENCE — what a worker's confirmation receipt is

plan.md:21029

**Why it is open**

**The whole question is one sentence: is the worker-side receipt UI state, or the worker's own copy of
evidence?** Everything else follows, and the lane deliberately left it unanswered rather than picking the
cheap one.
**The costs invert against intuition, which is why this needs a person.** The cheap contract reads the
**mutable** store — and that store *is* uniquely indexed. The evidence-grade contract reads the
**append-only** store — and that one is **not**. So the safer-sounding choice is the one carrying the
outstanding index and migration work.
**It is not a § 8-5-6 record either way.** The personalliste artifact comes from three other tables, and the
worker surface carries no statutory reference today. **C6 bites only if a UI string starts calling this row
personalliste evidence** — which is a thing either option could do wrongly.

**The options**

- `ui-state-one-column`
  - **pro:** the read already loads the row and stops one column short, so this is a field on an existing model and nearly free, and it survives a reload today
  - **con:** it reads the store that is mutated in place, so what the worker sees is a value somebody could change without leaving a trace, which is not what evidence means
- `workers-own-evidence`
  - **pro:** it reads the append-only receipts table, which is a new row per confirmation and therefore the thing an inspector would accept
  - **con:** that table has no unique index on its natural key and its race test is expected-red pending the duplicate-migration ruling, so this option queues behind that one and owes a second migration besides

Ruled: ui-state-one-column 2026-08-06 by @sven

Reopen when: an inspector or a labour dispute asks a worker to produce their own confirmation, at which point the mutable store is not evidence and the append-only read is owed with its index
